title: Butylchlorogenate from Chaenomeles speciosa alleviates ulcerative colitis via suppressing NLRP3 inflammasome activation and remodeling intestinal homeostasis.
authors: Huang, Jiaqi; Liu, Zhenqiang; Liu, Yingbo; Liu, Xinying; Tian, Zexi; Yao, Ming; Wang, Weidong; Liu, Zenggen
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 该文研究天然产物丁基绿原酸通过靶向NLRP3蛋白治疗溃疡性结肠炎，核心是蛋白-小分子互作而非蛋白质-DNA互作，且无AI或物理模拟方法用于TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Ulcerative colitis (UC) is a chronic inflammatory disease of the gastrointestinal tract. Despite the availability of traditional clinical treatments, their limitations highlight the need for alternative therapies derived from natural products that offer both strong efficacy and minimal side effects. Chaenomeles speciosa (Sweet) Nakai (CS), edible and medicinal fruit traditionally used to treat gastrointestinal disorders, has shown potential in UC management. However, the specific phytochemicals and mechanisms through which CS exerts its therapeutic effects remain poorly understood. PURPOSE: This study aimed to isolate and identify the bioactive compounds in CS, screen for the most potent compounds, especially chlorogenic acid derivatives, and assess their efficacy in treating UC. Additionally, we sought to investigate the underlying mechanisms of action. METHODS: The anti-inflammatory components from CS were separated and identified using various chromatographic techniques and nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy. Compounds with potential anti-inflammatory activity were screened using the NO release assay and enzyme linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Potential therapeutic pathways were explored through network pharmacology. In vivo, the therapeutic effect of the target compound, 3-O-(E)-caffeoylquinic acid n-butylester (BE), on UC was evaluated by monitoring body weight, disease activity index (DAI), colon length, histopathological scores, tight junction protein expression, and inflammatory marker transcript levels. Moreover, surface plasmon resonance (SPR) assay, gene knockdown, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations, quantitative Real-Time reverse transcription (qRT-PCR), and western blot (WB) analysis were employed to validate therapeutic mechanisms. The effects of BE on the intestinal microbiota and its associated metabolites in UC mice were further characterized through metagenomic sequencing and Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry (GC-MS). RESULTS: After preliminary activity investigation of isolated phenolic compounds based on ELISA, chlorogenic acid and its derivatives (BE and the novel 3-O-(Z)-caffeoylquinic acid n-butylester) were selected for CCK-8 assay and NO release inhibition. Among them, BE exhibited the most potent anti-inflammatory effects and was chosen for further intervention in UC mice. Network pharmacology analysis predicted that the NF-kappaB signaling pathway is a potential mechanism underlying the therapeutic effects of BE in UC. In vivo, BE effectively restored body weight and colon length, reduced DAI and histopathological scores, preserved the intestinal epithelial barrier, and decreased the expression of inflammatory biomarkers. WB and qRT-PCR experiments validated the BE attenuates inflammation by affecting the NF-kappaB/NLRP3 signaling pathway. SPR assay, gene knockdown, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics simulations revealed that BE inhibits activation of NLRP3 inflammasome by binding to NLRP3. Additionally, metagenomic sequencing and GC-MS showed that BE significantly reduced the relative abundance of Escherichia coli, while increasing Eubacterium and Roseburia sp. 1XD42-69. BE also restored short-chain fatty acid levels. CONCLUSION: Our findings suggest that BE, derived from CS, demonstrates promising therapeutic efficacy against UC. It exerts potent anti-UC effects by targeting NLRP3 and affecting the NF-kappaB/NLRP3 signaling axis to inhibit activation of NLRP3 inflammasome and remodeling intestinal homeostasis.
abstract_zh: 背景：溃疡性结肠炎（UC）是一种胃肠道的慢性炎症性疾病。尽管已有传统临床治疗方法，但其局限性凸显了从天然产物中开发兼具强效和低副作用替代疗法的必要性。木瓜（Chaenomeles speciosa (Sweet) Nakai, CS）是一种可食用且药用的果实，传统上用于治疗胃肠道疾病，在UC管理中显示出潜力。然而，CS发挥其治疗作用的具体植物化学物质及其机制仍知之甚少。目的：本研究旨在分离并鉴定CS中的生物活性化合物，筛选最有效的化合物，尤其是绿原酸衍生物，并评估其治疗UC的疗效。此外，我们试图探究其潜在的作用机制。方法：利用多种色谱技术和核磁共振波谱法分离并鉴定CS中的抗炎成分。通过NO释放试验和酶联免疫吸附试验（ELISA）筛选具有潜在抗炎活性的化合物。通过网络药理学探索潜在的治疗途径。在体内，通过监测体重、疾病活动指数（DAI）、结肠长度、组织病理学评分、紧密连接蛋白表达和炎症标志物转录水平，评估目标化合物3-O-(E)-咖啡酰奎宁酸正丁酯（BE）对UC的治疗效果。此外，采用表面等离子体共振（SPR）试验、基因敲低、分子对接、分子动力学模拟、定量实时逆转录（qRT-PCR）和蛋白质印迹（WB）分析来验证治疗机制。通过宏基因组测序和气相色谱-质谱联用（GC-MS）进一步表征BE对UC小鼠肠道微生物群及其相关代谢物的影响。结果：基于ELISA对分离的酚类化合物进行初步活性研究后，选择绿原酸及其衍生物（BE和新颖的3-O-(Z)-咖啡酰奎宁酸正丁酯）进行CCK-8试验和NO释放抑制试验。其中，BE表现出最强的抗炎作用，并被选作进一步干预UC小鼠的候选物。网络药理学分析预测NF-kappaB信号通路是BE在UC中治疗效果的潜在机制。在体内，BE有效恢复体重和结肠长度，降低DAI和组织病理学评分，保护肠上皮屏障，并减少炎症生物标志物的表达。WB和qRT-PCR实验验证了BE通过影响NF-kappaB/NLRP3信号通路来减轻炎症。SPR试验、基因敲低、分子对接和分子动力学模拟揭示，BE通过结合NLRP3抑制NLRP3炎症小体的激活。此外，宏基因组测序和GC-MS显示，BE显著降低大肠杆菌的相对丰度，同时增加真杆菌属和罗斯氏菌属sp. 1XD42-69。BE还恢复了短链脂肪酸水平。结论：我们的研究结果表明，源自CS的BE在治疗UC方面显示出有前景的疗效。它通过靶向NLRP3并影响NF-kappaB/NLRP3信号轴，抑制NLRP3炎症小体的激活并重塑肠道稳态，从而发挥强效的抗UC作用。
